A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hard-Spurious-ImageNet study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet bias measurements, benchmark accuracies, robustness experiments, saliency analyses, and appendix experiments using SAM and Grounding DINO.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds aspect-ratio-preserving evaluations, model-scale and training-strategy comparisons, and clean-accuracy measurements after robustness training.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds an alternative dataset-construction procedure that preserves object aspect ratio, limits oversized crops to the canvas, and selects corners randomly. The underlying cropping, inpainting, and compositing pipeline remains unchanged, as do the evaluated robustness algorithms.

E1.justification: v2 adds a test scenario with preserved object aspect ratios and randomized corners within the retained ImageNet classification task. The original dataset, ten-class subset, and SAM-mask evaluations remain; Hard-Spurious-ImageNet-10 is the renamed Hard-Spurious-ImageNet-v2, not a new class collection.

E2.justification: v2 adds EVA-CLIP, ViT-Tiny/Small/Large, and DeiT-Small comparisons. Its CLIP ViT-B/32 evaluation differs from v1's WIT-400M-pretrained, ImageNet-fine-tuned ViT-Base comparison, which is no longer reported. The original five benchmark architectures and ERM, JTT, and DFR comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include aspect-ratio-preserving resizing with randomized corners, class-name prompting for CLIP, ViT scaling from 5.7M to 307M parameters, a roughly parameter-matched training-strategy comparison, and clean-data evaluation after robustness training. The benchmark ConvNeXt pretraining description changes from ImageNet-21k/22k followed by ImageNet-1k fine-tuning to ImageNet-1k-only. Existing split counts and robustness-training hyperparameters remain unchanged; these reported changes do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of the combined aspect-ratio/corner modification, model scaling, DeiT versus ViT training, and clean-accuracy costs of robustness training. The original augmentation, ERM training-duration and group-balance analyses, GradCAM examples, SAM comparison, and Grounding DINO annotation check remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark results. Point-estimate reporting and the existing Kendall and Spearman correlation analyses remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new variants and model comparisons and revises existing benchmark and augmentation scores. For example, ConvNeXt's original-set 56-pixel CoR accuracy changes from 14.98% in v1 Table 5 to 7.12% in v2 Table 1, alongside changed declared pretraining, so this is not an established same-setting decline. Table 6 newly reports clean accuracies of 65.78%, 40.06%, and 69.25% for ERM, JTT, and DFR while retaining their synthetic-data scores. Ten-class and SAM group scores are retained.

T1.justification: The centeredness and size definitions in Equations 1–2 remain mathematically unchanged. v2 adds an intuitive explanation for choosing the infinity norm, but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: ImageNet has position and size biases, these interact with background reliance, the proposed benchmark exposes this vulnerability, and existing robustness approaches remain insufficient. Added experiments support rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning distortion-related difficulty, ImageNet fine-tuning as an explanation for the EVA/CLIP gap, limited benefits from distillation, and the clean-versus-robustness tradeoff. It removes v1's augmentation-based explanation for ConvNeXt's superiority. Section 3.3 also changes 'small' to 'large' objects despite unchanged negative correlations, introducing an inconsistent interpretation. The stated limitations in Section 6 remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Where v1 promises dataset-generation code, v2 reports dataset and implementation availability and supplies a repository link. It documents the new resizing rule and model/prompt configurations. Section 5.6 repeats existing appendix hyperparameters, and Table 11 summarizes previously stated sample counts rather than introducing new settings.

R1.justification: Related work expands the discussion of Waterbirds and ImageNet-9, explicitly contrasting their scope with the full ImageNet class set and joint size/location analysis. It adds self-supervised masking and concept-bottleneck references, plus citations supporting new model comparisons. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 renames the ten-class variant, expands selected related-work and robustness-method explanations, and reorganizes experimental subsections. Implementation details also appear in the main text, and appendices receive lettered headings. Much of the original narrative and overall section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column journal format. Figures are rearranged and merged, including v1 Figures 2–3 into v2 Figure 2 and multiple appendix figures into composite displays. Benchmark tables move into the main text and gain paired original/AR columns; new comparison tables, a clean-accuracy column, and a dataset-count table substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful geometric-sensitivity and model comparisons, exposes clean-accuracy costs, and supplies resource-access information. However, unlike v1, its ResNet-50 subgroup results no longer reconcile with the reported Hard aggregate: v2 Table 1 implies 25.56% under the stated grouping, while Table 6 retains 16.54%, without explaining different conditions. Section 3.3 also reverses 'small' to 'large' despite unchanged correlations. These empirical gains and new consistency problems leave the net quality change uncertain.
